slots.label: Hard-points and states sheet
slots.description: A two-page specification of the platform coordinates, living targets, inventory rules, three trailer states, exterior wording and proposed materials.

slots.label: Integrated trailer architecture
slots.description: One architecture board locating the shell, entry, glazing, ventilation, furniture, equipment bays and support attachments.

slots.label: Whole-trailer exterior perspectives
slots.description: One exterior board with front-left and rear-right perspectives of the developed NEST T2 body.

slots.label: Dimensioned orthographic package
slots.description: One package board containing top, positive-Y side and rear orthographic views with fixed coordinates and deployed-part envelopes.

slots.label: Interior plans, sections and perspectives
slots.description: One interior board combining DAY and NIGHT plans, longitudinal and transverse sections and two interior perspectives.

slots.label: Furniture conversion and openings
slots.description: One mechanism board covering seat-to-bed conversion, removable components, entry and window hardware, ventilation and folding-step movement.

slots.label: Equipment access and eleven-item retention
slots.description: One equipment board detailing eleven restrained travel locations, clearance dimensions, cool-box access and the manual water-handling sequence.

slots.label: TRAVEL state
slots.description: One stationary TRAVEL image on neutral studio ground with the cropped tow interface, closed exterior and a cutaway of secured contents.

slots.label: PARK state
slots.description: One campsite PARK image showing DAY furniture, entry access, grounded supports and deployed C1/C2.

slots.label: NIGHT state
slots.description: One campsite NIGHT image with two adults on unfolded R1/R2, the parked supports and a cutaway of retained equipment.

slots.label: NIGHT-to-TRAVEL pack-up sequence
slots.description: One pack-up board tracing furniture conversion, all eleven items, chock retrieval and the closed TRAVEL result.

slots.label: Final colour, material and finish schedule
slots.description: A two-page final schedule of exact colours, material locations, exterior-light functions and pending development checks.

slots.label: Twelve-second state-transition video
slots.description: One 12-second video of the delivered trailer and its furniture and inventory arrangements across TRAVEL, PARK and NIGHT.

slots.label: Integrated trailer design presentation
slots.description: A presentation of at least 10 pages reusing the specification and developed architecture, trailer views, mechanisms, retention, states, pack-up and final materials.

items.item: The developed views describe one shell, cabin, opening arrangement, furniture system and equipment installation derived from the integrated architecture.
Interior functions, opening movements and retained inventory fit the fixed platform bounds, exclusions and attachment locations recorded in the specification.
The scenes and sequence retain the developed shell, hinges, windows, wheel enclosures, furniture and eleven-item retention scheme while changing only the required state arrangements.
PARK, NIGHT and campsite pack-up share the supplied site and coordinate frame, and every removable component has a traceable destination through conversion and travel stowage.

Visible shell, protective band, running gear, furniture and cushions consistently apply the schedule's selected colour families, tones and material assignments, allowing changes caused by scene lighting.
Exterior wording and lighting locations remain consistent across the developed exterior and state scenes, with active lamps off in TRAVEL, PARK and NIGHT.

requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

Require two pages recording the client coordinate frame, platform geometry, living targets, inventory rules, state definitions, exterior copy and proposed material families. Verify the closed-total bounds X=-1850..2950/Y=-1200..1200/Z=0..2450, shell bounds X=-1850..1750/Y=-1050..1050/Z=450..2450, interior limits X=-1750..1650/Y=-950..950/Z=550..2350, both wheel exclusions, coupling-clearance box and low-equipment zone against the supplied tables. Verify axle points (0,+/-1000,300), coupling (2850,0,450), drawbar endpoints (1300,+/-700,450), front stabilizers (1300,+/-850,420), rear stabilizers (-1500,+/-850,420) and jockey reference (2300,0,400). Include two 600-diameter, 180-wide main tyres, the 200-diameter jockey wheel and its deployed centre Z=100. Living, inventory and state records must preserve the supplied values and uses, including DAY as parked seating. Equivalent notation is acceptable; missing categories, altered fixed values or contradictory state definitions fail.

The board must spatially locate the developed shell, positive-Y entry, opening window, high vent, two-seat accommodation, meal and preparation surfaces, bed conversion, equipment bays and every support attachment. Relationships must be understandable as one cabin with trailer-contained sleeping, storage and luggage provision. Diagram style and body form are open; disconnected component illustrations without their installed locations fail.

Use the verified specification and dimensioned views to establish one coordinate-consistent platform across these images: single axle, two main tyres, fixed A-frame endpoints and coupling, four stabilizer attachments and one retractable jockey wheel. The package must repeat the closed envelope, coupling coordinates and three state names. Shell and interior development must respect their recorded bounds, wheel exclusions and coupling-clearance occupancy, which is reserved for necessary coupling and drawbar hardware. Openings and attachments must correspond across views and states. Body styling and cabin layout may vary from the blank reference; moving fixed hard points, intersecting exclusions or introducing inconsistent openings fails.

Require both specified opposing perspectives, together explaining the complete developed trailer exterior and its proportions. Rendering technique is open; a missing perspective or views that conceal the overall body configuration fail.

Require dimensioned top, entry-side and rear orthographic views that agree with one another. They must locate the coupling, fixed exclusion volumes and the occupied envelopes of deployed parts in the stated coordinate frame. Labels, overlays or separate deployment diagrams are acceptable; perspective-only evidence, absent exclusions or unexplained deployment extents fail.

The interior and furniture boards must provide legible dimensional evidence for a flat bed with X length at least 1950 and Y width at least 1400, bed top no higher than Z=1150 and at least 800 clear above it. Require exactly two usable seats, each at least 450 wide and deep, cushion height 400..470 above floor, and a 650x500 meal surface with top 650..750 above floor. Show an internal cold-meal preparation surface, a DAY entry-to-preparation route at least 550 wide and a reachable NIGHT bed edge connecting to the entry. NIGHT and pack-up must use the same furniture and identify the locations of all removable panels and cushions. Alternative conversion mechanisms are allowed; dimensional shortfalls, inaccessible routes or components disappearing between arrangements fail.

Require both functional plans, both section orientations and two interior perspectives. All views must describe the same cabin, with enough visibility to understand daytime meals, preparation, storage and sleeping. Graphic treatment is open; missing views or mutually incompatible layouts fail.

Trace an understandable seat-to-bed conversion and assign each removable furniture component a named place in DAY, NIGHT and TRAVEL. Show entry and opening-window hinges, latches, opening paths and travel closure, the high ventilation opening and both folding-step treads through deployment and stowage. The window must serve seating or sleeping use, and openings must align with interior functions and clear fixed exclusions. Exploded diagrams and sequential details are acceptable; unexplained movement, missing hardware or an unlocated loose component fails.

Dimensioned evidence must establish one positive-Y entry with clear X width at least 600, clear Z height at least 1650 and sill at most 30 above floor, plus treads at absolute Z=180 and 360. Compare its actual movement and closure with the state depictions. PARK, NIGHT and campsite stages of pack-up must keep the body, opened parts, supports, step and actors within X=-2500..3650, Y=-2000..3300 and Z<=3100, preserving the Y=1250..2750 entry-side access band and a route at least 550 wide around the deployed door and step. TRAVEL must stow deployable living and support parts within the closed-total envelope with their undersides at least 250 above ground. Viewpoint may change; coordinate shifts, blocked access, protruding travel parts or unsupported dimensional claims fail.

Require eleven separately identified, nonoverlapping retained travel places with restraints, support beneath and at least 10 clearance at each side, each end and overhead. Check occupied envelopes: E1 480x320x360; E2/E3 each 200x180x300; E4 300x240x100; E5 380x280x250; P1/P2 each 450x280x200; C1/C2 each 180x120x100; R1/R2 each rolled axial length 700 and diameter 280, retained in 720x300x290. Rigid boxes remain upright; a labelled 90-degree plan rotation is allowed. Entire retained envelopes of E1/E2/E3 must lie in X=-650..650/Y=-700..700/Z=550..1050. Show passive E1 with DAY lid access, separate upright E2 FRESH and E3 WASTE, and manual transfer from fresh container through E4 on the internal preparation surface to waste container. E5 remains one cold-food crate and both bags retain full occupied volumes. TRAVEL and pack-up must account for all eleven items with empty capped E2/E3 and empty retained E4; NIGHT must show two separate 1950x700x30 unfolded bedding pieces and assigned locations for remaining equipment and luggage. Missing IDs, shared occupied bays, undersized envelopes or an incompatible use sequence fail.

PARK and NIGHT must show ground contact for both main tyres, all four 120x120 stabilizer pads and the deployed jockey wheel, with C1 touching the front of the positive-Y tyre and C2 touching the rear of the opposite tyre. PARK has entry and step open with DAY furniture available. NIGHT has the entry closed, step deployed and high vent open. TRAVEL and the final pack-up result have raised stabilizers and jockey wheel, internally retained chocks, stowed step and closed doors, windows and vents. Earlier pack-up stages may retain the support and opening positions appropriate to their stage. Cutaways or clear supplementary views may resolve occlusion; incorrect contacts, reversed chocks or incompatible state positions fail.

Show a level stationary trailer on neutral flat studio ground, coupled at the fixed reference to a neutral cropped tow-interface stub. The cabin must be unoccupied, and a cutaway must reveal secured contents in their assigned arrangement. Cutaway styling is open; a moving scene, occupied cabin, missing coupling interface or hidden travel retention fails.

Show the unhitched trailer on the supplied flat campsite with the two-place DAY arrangement available, including the meal table and internal preparation provision. Entry access, deployed supports and both chocks must be visibly assessable. Perspective and evening-light interpretation may vary; a substituted setting, unavailable DAY furniture or concealed chocks fails.

Show exactly two adults lying on the developed bed, with R1 and R2 unfolded, at the same campsite and parked footprint as PARK. A cutaway must reveal the assigned retained equipment and luggage without replacing the established cabin arrangement. Camera position may change; missing occupants, sleeping outside the cabin, rolled NIGHT bedding or an absent equipment cutaway fails.

Provide an ordered, traceable sequence from NIGHT to DAY, through return of every removable furniture component and all eleven portable items to their named travel locations, retrieval of both chocks, support and jockey-wheel retraction, step stowage and closure of openings. Use the supplied campsite for pack-up and neutral flat ground for the final tow-ready depiction. Shell, hinges, windows, wheel enclosures, furniture and retention scheme must remain consistent with the source work. Panel count is open; skipped required actions, disappearing items or a final arrangement incompatible with TRAVEL fails.

Require two pages recording exact selected tones and finishes with location assignments: warm off-white aluminium-faced composite main shell; muted forest green coated composite lower band; graphite wheel parts and steel underframe; light natural wood birch-faced plywood furniture; warm grey recycled PET upholstery; coordinated anti-slip rubber floor; transparent glazing with detailed selection open. Identify locations and functions for two red tail/brake assemblies, two amber rear turn units, two passive red rear reflectors and two white forward position lamps, and specify active state-scene lamps OFF. List structure, towing, support, restraint, conversion, ventilation, sealing and user-fit checks as pending. Exact tones and detailing are designer choices; omitted assignments, changed required families or claims that pending checks are already validated fail.

Each target must show the required product name and descriptor on the positive-Y exterior body, with colour and material assignments matching the final schedule wherever those surfaces are visible. The exterior board must locate all eight specified lighting and reflector elements with correct colour and function; labelled details may supplement the perspectives. Active lamps must be visibly off in all three state scenes, while passive reflectors may reflect ambient light. Natural lighting shifts and cutaway conventions are allowed; copy placed only in a page title, mismatched material families, missing lighting units or illuminated active state lamps fail.

Require at least ten pages that repeat the 4800x2400x2450 closed envelope, coupling reference X=2850/Y=0/Z=450 and TRAVEL/PARK/NIGHT names, plus the final colour and material selections with their locations. Reproduced exterior imagery must carry the name and descriptor on the entry-side body. Identify any design refinements and the affected source work so their propagation can be traced; no refinements need be invented when the design is unchanged. Page layout and narrative order are open; contradictory facts, obsolete material choices, missing body copy or unexplained changes fail.

The presentation must visibly reuse identifiable material from every listed source, including all three state images and both written specifications. Cropping, scaling and rearrangement are acceptable when the source design and relevant information remain recognizable. Merely naming a source, replacing it with unrelated new imagery or omitting any source fails.

Review the entire 12-second video for labelled TRAVEL, PARK and NIGHT and recognizable reuse of the delivered trailer, furniture and inventory arrangement. Preserve the axle, A-frame, support attachments, openings and conversion system throughout. TRAVEL must be stationary and coupled on neutral ground, unoccupied, with secured inventory, raised supports and jockey wheel, retained chocks and closed openings. PARK must be unhitched at the campsite with DAY furniture, open entry and deployed step. PARK and NIGHT require grounded tyres, four pads and jockey wheel with correctly positioned C1/C2; NIGHT requires closed entry, deployed step, open high vent, two adults on unfolded bedding and remaining contents retained. Active exterior lamps remain off. Editing and transition style are open; incorrect duration, missing state labels, incompatible state arrangements or unexplained product changes fail.
